pages.title: HTTP API Route Registry
pages.purpose: Domain-grouped reference of every documented API route: runtimes, mcp (+catalog), skills (+skills-sh search/install SSE), plugins (+marketplace), processes, sessions (+reply), prompts, settings, tools (action/diagnose/dashboard/job/usage), workspaces (+clone), memory (docs/openwiki/graphify/runtimes/file/visualizer), and the /dashboard/* Headroom embed proxy - with each route's role and whether it mutates state.
instructions: Group routes by domain tables as in architecture.md; explicitly mark mutating routes (they must follow the file-first saveState + invalidateDashboardCache discipline) and SSE routes (job streams read file logs).

Note the SSRF/security properties attached to specific routes (clone host filter, memory/file allowlist, dashboard proxy literal upstream) as pointers into the security-model page rather than duplicating it.

pages.title: Console Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: System-level picture of the Agentic OS Console: Bun-workspace Next.js 15 / React 19 / zustand stack, client-server-core-adapter layering, data flow over RSC/JSON/SSE, the three sources of truth (vendor runtime configs, state.json, server-driven UI data), the core mutation invariant (file first, then client), and the performance mechanisms (dashboard micro-cache with TTL+dedup, single-ps snapshot, scanLimit, tabCache, streaming skeletons).
instructions: Embed a mermaid flowchart showing the layer stack (pages/components/store → API routes → src/core modules → runtime adapters → FS/ps/headless-CLI) grounded in architecture.md's ASCII diagram.
Keep the performance table (core/cache.ts TTL 5s + dedup, ps-snapshot TTL 2s, scanLimit, tabCache, loading.tsx) as a compact reference - these mechanisms recur on many pages.

List the key invariants verbatim-level: runtime list truth is .agents/runtime/<vendor>/config.json (console only reads), console state is .agents/console/state.json outside git, UI runtime plugins are presentation-only.

pages.title: Security Model and Guard Boundaries
pages.purpose: Cross-cutting security rules an agent must obey when changing the console: SSRF-filtered server fetches (scheme/host allowlists, private-range bans, timeouts, size caps), literal-command spawn discipline with argument arrays and no shells (Mimosa pre-commit blocks spawn wrappers as injection patterns), prompt and package/MCP-name sanitization, the memory file read allowlist (checkReadPath: markdown in workspaces, openwiki/ and runtime memory dirs, realpath containment, no hidden components, 1 MB cap), the guard write boundary (console writes only .agents/console/ + managed MCP configs; never runtime configs or skill files), embed-proxy constraints, and secrets exclusion from git.
instructions: Embed a mermaid flowchart of the checkReadPath decision chain (absolute path → allowed roots → realpath containment → hidden-component ban → extension/size cap).
Per repo guidance: when validating security-relevant behavior, prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior and preserve complete failure output.

State the non-obvious rules explicitly: never introduce wrapper functions around spawn (inline switch over literal commands is the approved pattern), prompts are sanitized for NUL/length/leading dash, plugin installs are resolved by id from trusted catalogs only.

pages.title: Console State and Persistence
pages.purpose: The .agents/console/state.json persistence model: full schema (mcp, skills, defaultRuntime, settings.taskRuntimes, plugins, workspaces, tools, lastMcpSync), atomic tmp+rename writes, merge-on-defaults reads so a missing/broken file never crashes the console, ~/ expansion via expandHome, validation rules (openwiki/graphify subsets of workspaces), the mutation ordering invariant (mutate → saveState → response → client store; store never leads the file), cache invalidation on every mutation, and the adjacent side files (package-manager.json, tools.env, tools-usage.json, dashboards.json, tool-jobs/, logs/, runs/) with their distinct formats.
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of the mutation flow (API route → state mutation → saveState tmp+rename → invalidateDashboardCache → response → zustand store update).

Include the JSONC schema block from architecture.md and the per-section ownership notes (who reads/writes each section); call out that state.json is machine-local (paths belong to this machine, .agents/console/ is gitignored).

pages.title: MCP Registry and Sync Semantics
pages.purpose: The console-owned MCP registry: the effective-enabledness formula (runtimeOverrides[R] ?? enabled), toggle semantics (remove from target files, keep the registry entry for one-click restore), transport editing (stdio command/args/env, http url/headers - transport replaced wholesale on PATCH), the managed-names ownership model (each target owns current-registry ∪ previously-applied names, so foreign entries survive and departed servers are cleaned), and the mutation→syncMcp→lastMcpSync→saveState→cache-invalidation pipeline with per-target results surfaced in the UI.
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of the change flow: UI/API mutation → registry update → syncMcp across targets → lastMcpSync results → saveState (file first) → invalidateDashboardCache → client response.

Explain the managed-names bug class (server leaving the registry would linger in target files forever without the ∪-with-last-applied rule, caught by live plugin round-trip) - it is the invariant most likely to be broken by refactors.

pages.title: MCP Sync Targets and Native Formats
pages.purpose: Reference for every sync target and its native format: project .mcp.json, claude-user via `claude mcp add-json/remove -s user` with ~/.claude.json merge fallback, codex-global via the section-based TOML editor (lib/toml.ts), cursor-global mcp.json, opencode-global jsonc (type local/remote), zcode/kimi as project-only, plus the header-support matrix per target, the MCP_PRESETS catalog (Context7, DeepWiki, WebMCP, Playwright; serena/qmd/codegraph tool presets) and the bunx↔npx adaptation to the configured package manager without overwriting installed servers.
instructions: Keep the target/format table and the stdio-vs-http examples (JSON and TOML) verbatim-level; they are the contract third-party refactors must preserve.
Note that headers are supported only by JSON targets (.mcp.json, Cursor, Claude fallback); opencode remote and Codex TOML write url only - an easy detail to regress.

pages.title: Plugins and Marketplace Catalogs
pages.purpose: The plugin system: PluginDef bundles (id, mcp contributions, declared skills, source) whose enabled state physically moves MCP servers into or out of the shared registry (with the transport-compare safeguard that protects user-modified servers from being removed on disable), the builtin chrome-devtools plugin, marketplace JSON manifests with server-side validation/normalization, the trusted-catalog install rule (lookup by id from builtin + added marketplaces, never from request bodies), and the marketplace SSRF protections (https-only, private-range host bans, 10s timeout, 512KB cap).
instructions: Call out that DELETE = disable + record removal, and that the live round-trip bug (servers surviving plugin disable) motivated the managed-names model documented in mcp pages.
Show the PluginDef interface and a manifest example; make the enable→registry→sync / disable→transport-compare→remove cycle explicit as a mermaid flowchart.

pages.title: Runtime Activity, Statuses, Diagnostics and Awaiting-Input
pages.purpose: The runtime health model: per-runtime repo-scope and machine-scope activity signals (mtime traces, rollout correlation, sqlite freshness), the status ladder (active-now ≤5min → recently-active windows → inactive, plus disabled/unknown), the issues system (common checks: unverified models, MCP sync errors; adapter checks: guard hook file, AGENT_RUNTIME link, zcode hooks.enabled, cursor fail-open, Kimi mirrored [[hooks]], OpenCode plugin) surfacing as ⚠ badges with the "Исправить" fix path, and the awaiting-input heuristic (completed turn + file silent ≥2 min + processes alive) with per-runtime detection specifics.
instructions: Embed a mermaid stateDiagram-v2 of the status ladder (disabled/unknown/inactive/recently-active/active-now) with the timing thresholds as transitions.
Keep the per-runtime signal table and the awaiting-input heuristics table - they are the tables agents consult when adding or fixing an adapter.

pages.title: Runtime Adapter System
pages.purpose: How the six agent runtimes (Claude Code, Codex CLI, ZCode, Cursor, Kimi, OpenCode) plug into the console: .agents/runtime/<id>/config.json as the discovery source of truth, the RuntimeAdapter interface (probeSignals, isInstalled, detectIssues, awaitingInput, listSkills/listSessions/getSession, replyCommand/runCommand - all optional except identity), ProbeContext with FsSignalHelpers as the only FS access, ADAPTERS registration, client UI plugins (monogram/color only), and the 5-step recipe for adding a new runtime.
instructions: Keep the 'add a new runtime' checklist (config.json → adapter file → ADAPTERS line → optional UI plugin → docs table updates in the same commit series per AGENTS.md §11) as an actionable recipe.
Present the RuntimeAdapter interface as a method-by-method table with what each hook feeds on the dashboard; emphasize adapters never touch the FS directly (only via FsSignalHelpers) for testability.

pages.title: Session History, Filtering and Headless Replies
pages.purpose: Session introspection across runtimes: per-runtime session sources (claude projects jsonl with dashed-slug workspace mapping, codex rollout session_meta cwd peek, kimi session_index + state.json, zcode rollout↔plan correlation, sqlite-based cursor/opencode honestly marked unsupported), workspace-folder filtering semantics, preview extraction (head/tail chunk helpers, ~30 entry transcripts), and the headless resume mechanism (per-runtime reply commands, 120s timeout, cwd = session dir, separate process that never touches the user's interactive session).
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of the reply flow (session view → POST /api/sessions/reply → adapter replyCommand → detached CLI spawn with literal command → output to UI).

Keep the resume-command and session-source tables verbatim-level; note new-session prompt commands (claude -p, codex exec, etc.) cross-reference the runtime-operations page rather than duplicating it.

pages.title: Skill Levels and Toggle Overlays
pages.purpose: The skill model: the three levels shown in a runtime space (Runtime Skills from per-runtime directories, Harness Skills from .agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md, Scripts for non-skill agents/plugins/prompts, plus the per-runtime MCP override tab), and the overlay precedence formula effective = runtimeOverrides[skill][R] ?? defaults[skill] ?? useGlobal, with the core principle that the console never modifies skill files - every toggle is a state.json overlay applied file-first.
instructions: List the per-runtime skill directory sources (claude ~/.claude/skills, ZCode plugin cache, ~/.cursor/skills-cursor, ~/.codex/skills, Kimi extra_skill_dirs) as the adapter contract.
Present the effective() precedence as both the formula and a worked example; stress the 'file first, then UI' application order shared with all state mutations.

pages.title: skills.sh Search, Install, Remove and Creation
pages.purpose: The skills.sh lifecycle end to end: search via `bunx skills find` CLI parsing (owner/repo@skill ids, 60s cache, HTTP fallback under 3 results), the detail-description chain (registry snapshot → og:description → GitHub page → DeepWiki → iframe fallback, 5-min cache) plus security audit sources, install as an SSE-streamed job (`bunx skills add -y` into .agents/skills with agent-directory symlinks and skills-lock.json, stdin input route, pre-install audit modal), removal with CLI plus manual fallback cleanup, and skill creation via a prompt-builder that launches a headless session on the configured task runtime targeting .agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md.
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of the install flow (search result → audit modal → POST install → bunx skills add job → SSE stream from output → symlink/lock results in skill list).
Keep the CLI-output parse format and the DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 / repo-root-cwd spawn parameters exact; note SSRF rules that govern the description/audit fetches.

pages.title: tool.sh Dispatcher, Project Indexing and Pre-Commit Maintenance
pages.purpose: The agent-facing and maintenance side of context tools: the tooling/scripts/tool.sh dispatcher contract (status output, exit 0 vs exit 3 + TOOL_UNAVAILABLE hint, tools.env TOOL_<ID> state with which-fallback), setup.sh installation flow including safe external installers (downloaded to .agents/.tmp/setup/, no curl|bash), per-workspace project init/reinit for Serena/CodeGraph/Graphify (init/index/update command triples, initMarker detection), the husky pre-commit index refresh (best-effort, SKIP_TOOLS_UPDATE=1 escape hatch), and the artifact ignore policy (.codegraph/, graphify-out/ ignored; .serena/ committable).
instructions: Document the dispatcher contract exactly - exit 3 + 'TOOL_UNAVAILABLE <id>: <hint>' is the signal that tells agents to fall back to normal workflow; include the tool.sh status/run usage snippets.
Note that projectInit.update runs on every commit and must be fast and silent when uninitialized; Graphify --code-only needs no LLM key while full mode does.

pages.title: Developing Tool Plugins (ToolDef)
pages.purpose: Author guide for a new context-tool plugin: the full ToolDef field reference (systemInstall with globalInstallCommand pm-awareness, requires, mcpPreset, perRuntime supported/install/uninstall/markerFile/notes/params, detachedInstall + dashboardCommand for services, uninstallStopsDashboard, postInstallCommands, projectInit init/reinit/update/initMarker, dashboard), auto-derived diagnostics checks and the "Исправить" fix-prompt hookup, the nine-step same-commit-series checklist (core/tools.ts, tool.sh, setup.sh, docs/tools.md, AGENTS.md tables, core/__tests__/tools.test.ts, MCP preset, version-detection caveat), and the security limits (no shells, boundary-checked cleanup paths, literal job filenames, TCP-only dashboard liveness).
instructions: Per repo guidance: state that the required test (core/__tests__/tools.test.ts covering install/uninstall commands and the support matrix) should be validated with the narrowest quiet test run, preserving complete failure output.
Reproduce the ToolDef annotated structure and the checklist as the page backbone; emphasize spawn-without-shell literal arrays because guard/Mimosa enforce it.

pages.title: Context Tools Registry and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: The context-saving tool ecosystem managed by the console (Serena, qmd, CodeGraph, Graphify, RTK, Headroom, OpenWiki): the integration map (system package / MCP preset / per-runtime install / dashboard), ToolDef-plugin organization under core/tools/<id>.ts with the core/tools.ts aggregator, the lifecycle states missing→on→off with install/uninstall/reinstall/toggle actions and their quirks (optional uninstall steps, RTK programmatic project cleanup of marker blocks, Headroom uninstall-stops-dashboard, marker-based merge of external installs), the Bun/NPM package-manager choice, per-runtime unsupported matrix, dashboard embedding with autostart/lazy-lift, and the tools-usage.json statistics model.
instructions: Embed a mermaid stateDiagram-v2 of the lifecycle (missing → on → off) with action arrows labeled install/uninstall/reinstall/toggle.
Keep the integration-map and unsupported-matrix tables; reproduce the reinstall safety rules verbatim (uninstall failures must not break the chain; installed-record merges marker findings).

pages.title: Console UIKit and Layout Contract
pages.purpose: The UIKit contract for console screens: single source of primitives (apps/console/src/ui/UIKit.tsx), layout components (Page, PageHeader with actions slot, NavBar with isActive callback), controls (Button/IconButton variants and sizes, Toggle, Select replacing native selects with keyboard semantics, Input/Textarea, Segmented, Tabs with badges), containers and text (Panel, Modal, Notice, Chip tones, EmptyState, SectionLabel/FieldLabel/Footnote), confirmDialog via the single UIKitHost, utility hooks (cx, useClickOutside), and the extension rules (tone maps own colors, no native browser controls, lucide-react icons only, UIKit stays domain-free, docs updated in the same commit series).
instructions: Keep the component/props tables compact and reference-grade; include short usage snippets for Page composition and confirmDialog.

Restate the non-obvious rules that reviewers enforce: new primitives go into UIKit with a docblock (never styled ad hoc in screens), rounding/spacing come from size/variant props to avoid Tailwind class conflicts, Modal does not close on overlay click to protect forms.

pages.title: Install Jobs, SSE Streaming and Detached Processes
pages.purpose: The shared long-running-job pattern used across features: file-backed job logs (.agents/console/tool-jobs/<id>.log|.json) tailed by SSE routes so streams survive Next.js HMR and route-bundle boundaries, stdin input routes for interactive installers, skills.sh install jobs, tool install/reinstall jobs with dryRun preview, workspace clone job terminals, standalone dashboard instances (pid in dashboards.json, logs in logs/<id>-dashboard.log, autostart with lazy 30s-throttled lift), and detached build processes tracked by .console-build.json pid/mode files - the invariant being that no job state lives in in-memory Maps.
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of a generic job lifecycle (start → spawn detached writing file log → SSE route tails file → optional stdin input → status .json completion → cache invalidation).

Explain the HMR/bundle-boundary rationale for file-backed logs (in-memory Map is empty in the neighboring route bundle - the root cause of the 'waiting for output forever' bug) as the design invariant to preserve.

pages.title: Runtime Operations: Processes, Prompts and Task Settings
pages.purpose: Cross-system day-to-day control workflow: process management (ps filtered by adapter processPattern, app-vs-cli classification, stop SIGTERM→3s grace→SIGKILL with fresh-ps PID re-verification, restart for .app bundles only), headless prompt execution via POST /api/prompts/run with the runtime selection chain (explicit → settings.taskRuntimes.promptExecution → defaultRuntime ★), the Diagnostics "Исправить" button building fix prompts from issues (buildFixPrompt honoring AGENTS.md/guard), detached run logs under .agents/console/runs/, prompt sanitization, and the task-runtime settings page semantics.
instructions: Embed a mermaid flowchart of the prompt runtime-selection chain and a sequence diagram of the process-stop action (action request → fresh ps snapshot → PID verify → SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL).
Make explicit that the Fix button is disabled with a hint when no effective runtime is selected, and that the same prompt route serves skill creation via taskRuntimes.skillCreation.

pages.title: Workspaces and Memory (Docs, OpenWiki, Graphify, Runtime)
pages.purpose: Workspace-driven workflows: the workspaces model (exactly one mandatory folder + additional, absolute-path/exists/no-dup validation, ~ expansion) feeding session filtering and repo-scope activity signals; sources/ git-clone jobs with https-only SSRF host filtering; and the Memory tab reading everything from disk with no own storage - Docs tree rendering (limits 500 files/depth 8, auto-select README→AGENTS), OpenWiki builds via external CLI (openwiki --init/--update as detached processes with .console-build.json/.console-build.log status files and 4s polling, runtime-★ fallback when no LLM key), the static wiki-graph visualizer export/publish into public/visualizers/<sha256-slug>/, Graphify extract/update builds plus graph.html publish into public/graphify/<slug>/, per-runtime memory file sources, and the memory-file read allowlist.
instructions: Embed a mermaid sequence diagram of an OpenWiki build (UI build button → literal spawn openwiki --init/--update cwd=workspace → .console-build.json/.log status polling → iframe/viewer publish).

Note cross-cutting facts: build isolation per folder, slug = sha256 of workspace path for publishes, /api/memory/openwiki resyncs and cleans slugs, graph rendering needs internet CDN while builds are local.

pages.title: Quickstart: Agentic OS Console Docs Wiki
pages.purpose: Task-routing entry point. Explains that this repo is the documentation workspace of the harness / Agentic OS Console system (code lives in the parent monorepo apps/console, tooling/, .agents/), maps the wiki hierarchy (architecture / runtimes / mcp / skills / tools / workflows / ui), and routes common change tasks - add a runtime, add an MCP server or plugin, add a skill, add a context tool, change console UI, touch state.json or security-sensitive code - to the right pages.
instructions: Organize the quickstart as a task-routing table ('I want to change X' → wiki page), not a directory dump; route readers down the hierarchy into exactly one best starting page per task.
Per repo guidance: treat the documented behavior (backed by the parent repo's source and tests) as authoritative; unknowns in the docs are verification gaps, not requirements.

This repository contains only documentation (Russian-language) for the Agentic OS Console; referenced code paths such as apps/console/src/** and tooling/scripts/** belong to the parent harness monorepo - describe the system as documented here and keep those cross-repo references explicit instead of inventing source-level claims.
